commands.harvest.doc: Gathers the harvest from the tile under the drone. If the plant isn't ripe yet, it's lost and you get nothing (only wheat isn't lost: it just keeps growing).
commands.harvest.notes: Use isRipe() first to check that the plant is ripe.
commands.doAFlip.doc: The drone does a flip. It takes 1 second. Just for fun.
commands.playNote.doc: The drone plays with a warm piano sound. Use Notes.C, D, E, F, G, A, B, HighC, or a pitch in quotes: "C4", "C#4", "Bb3" (A0 to C8 covers all 88 piano keys). A list plays a chord of up to 8 notes together. Notes.Rest is silence. The second number is the length in beats, from 0.125 to 8; the default is 1. The optional third number is the tempo, from 30 to 300 beats per minute (BPM). Without it, one beat lasts half a second: 120 BPM.
commands.move.doc: The drone moves one tile: Up, Down, Right or Left. If it goes off the edge, it comes back on the other side.
commands.move.notes: In a maze you can't go through walls: check with canGo().
commands.canMove.doc: true if the drone can go that way (maze walls may block it).
commands.getWorldSize.doc: The size of the farm. For example, 3 if the farm is 3×3.
commands.plant.doc: Plants something under the drone. Plants are in the Plants group: Plants.Rosehip, Plants.Eggplant…
commands.plant.notes: The tile must be empty (wheat doesn't count). Some plants grow only in plowed soil.
commands.canHarvest.doc: true if the plant under the drone is ripe and ready to gather, otherwise false.
commands.canHarvest.notes: For a watermelon, true only means it has grown. scan() tells you whether it's sweet.
commands.getEntityType.doc: What's growing under the drone (for example, Plants.Wheat), or null if there's nothing.
commands.till.doc: Plows the ground. A meadow turns into plowed soil (Soils.Field), and plowed soil turns back into a meadow.
commands.getGroundType.doc: The kind of soil under the drone: Soils.Meadow or Soils.Field.
commands.getPosX.doc: The drone's column, counting from left to right (the first column is 0).
commands.getPosY.doc: The drone's row, counting from bottom to top (the first row is 0).
commands.numItems.doc: How much of that item you have. Items are in the Goods group: Goods.Wheat, Goods.Wood…
commands.print.doc: Writes values to the console, under the code window. Separate several values with commas. console.log() does the same.
commands.changeHat.doc: Gives the drone a new hat. Hats are in the Hats group.
commands.useItem.doc: Uses an item on the tile under the drone: water or humus. Magic dust is used only on maze treasure. You can leave out the amount (then it's 1).
commands.getWater.doc: How wet the soil under the drone is: from 0 (dry) to 1 (very wet).
commands.digPond.doc: Digs a pond under the drone (the plant there disappears). Fill it with water, and fish will show up. plow() fills the pond with soil again.
commands.digPond.notes: Pond water doesn't dry up. The pond is full when waterLevel() is 1.
commands.catchFish.doc: Catches a random fish in a full pond and returns it: Fish.Carp, Fish.Barbel, Fish.Ishkhan or Fish.Goldfish, in winter also Fish.Whitefish, and in the rain Fish.Catfish. The fish go to Storage.
commands.catchFish.notes: One cast takes a few seconds, and after a catch the pond rests a little. If there's no pond, or it isn't full, or it's resting, it returns null.
commands.getSeason.doc: Returns the current season: Seasons.Spring, Seasons.Summer, Seasons.Autumn or Seasons.Winter. The season is the same for all students.
commands.getSeason.notes: Every plant grows 2 times faster in its favorite season and 2 times slower in the others (see the "Plants" section).
commands.getWeather.doc: Returns the current weather: WeatherTypes.Sunny, WeatherTypes.Rain, WeatherTypes.Storm, WeatherTypes.Heat or WeatherTypes.Snow.
commands.getWeather.notes: Rain and storms water every tile and pond. In the heat, water dries up fast. Storm lightning makes a plant's harvest 3 times bigger.
commands.getNextWeather.doc: Returns the next weather, which starts in a few minutes (a weather forecast).
commands.getNextWeather.notes: Handy for planning ahead, for example to save water if rain is coming soon.
commands.build.doc: Builds a machine under the drone: Machines.Mill (water mill), Machines.JamPot (jam pot) or Machines.Tonir (tonir, a clay oven in the ground). The tile must be empty or have wheat.
commands.build.notes: Machines unlock with the village buildings. To remove a machine, use plow().
commands.make.doc: Starts making goods in the machine under the drone, taking the ingredients from Storage. The mill makes Goods.Flour, the jam pot Goods.Jam, and the tonir Goods.Lavash, Goods.Gata, Goods.Ghapama and Goods.GrilledFish.
commands.make.notes: When it's ready, isRipe() is true, and gather() takes it. See the recipes in the village.
commands.eat.doc: Eats one food from Storage and gives a boost for 30 seconds: Goods.Gata (the drone is 2 times faster), Goods.Ghapama (plants grow 2 times faster), Goods.GrilledFish (goldfish bite 3 times more often).
commands.eat.notes: Eating again makes the boost last longer.
commands.buildGreenhouse.doc: Covers the tile under the drone with glass. Under glass it's always the plant's favorite season, and rain, heat, frost and lightning can't get in.
commands.buildGreenhouse.notes: The glass stays forever, even after wipe(). Under glass you have to do the watering yourself.
commands.festivalDistance.doc: On festival days, tells you how many steps (left-right plus up-down) it is from the drone to the nearest hidden festival object. With no festival, it returns null.
commands.festivalDistance.notes: dig() digs the object up, but if you dig in the wrong spot, the nearest object runs away somewhere else, so find the right tile first. Unlocks with the Festival square.
commands.findTreasure.doc: Looks for a secret note's treasure under the drone. On the right tile it finds it (stars!) and returns true.
commands.findTreasure.notes: Careful: on the wrong tile the treasure vanishes and the note fails (the villagers may give it to you again). So solve the riddle first, then dig. Your notes are in Bridgy's Book, under "Notes".
commands.measure.doc: Measures a plant: an apricot tree's harvests left, a watermelon's sweetness (0–100), a pomegranate's seeds or a grape's sweetness (0–9). Without a direction, it measures under the drone. In a maze it gives the treasure's position, and for the snake, the mouse's.
commands.swap.doc: The grape under the drone and the grape next to it swap places. Works only along the row: Right or Left.
commands.getTickCount.doc: How many "steps" (ticks) the drone has made during this run.
commands.setSpeed.doc: Slows the drone down. speed(1) is the normal speed, speed(0.5) is half, speed(0) means no limit.
commands.getCost.doc: The price of the research's next level. For a plant, the price of planting it.
commands.unlock.doc: Buys the research right from your code. true if the purchase worked.
commands.clear.doc: Clears the whole farm and takes the drone to tile (0, 0).
commands.clear.notes: Careful: all the plants will be lost.
commands.drinkJuice.doc: The drone drinks one pomegranate juice and does its next 50 actions 2 times faster. Returns true if there was juice.
commands.spawnDrone.doc: Creates a new drone that runs the function you give it. Write the function's name without ().
commands.waitFor.doc: Waits until the drone finishes its work, and returns what its function returned.
commands.hasFinished.doc: true if the drone has already finished.
commands.numDrones.doc: How many drones are working right now.
commands.maxDrones.doc: The most drones you can have at the same time.
commands.Math.doc: Math functions: floor, ceil, round, abs, min, max, sqrt, pow …
commands.parseInt.doc: Turns text into a whole number.
commands.isNaN.doc: true if x is not a number.
commands.Object.doc: An object's keys, values or pairs: keys(), values(), entries().
commands.Array.doc: true if x is a list.
ranch.move.doc: The drone moves one tile inside its own area. The fence stops it (it doesn't come out on the other side).
ranch.canMove.doc: true if there's no fence that way.
ranch.getWorldSize.doc: The size of the drone's area (the henhouse is 4×4, so 4). x and y in an area start from 0.
ranch.getEntityType.doc: What's under the drone: an egg (Goods.Egg), a thing (Machines.FeedTrough, Machines.Well, Machines.Basket…), an animal (Animals.Hen) or null.
ranch.numItems.doc: How much is in the ranch storage: Goods.Dram, Goods.Egg, Goods.Milk, Goods.Grain, Goods.HayBale.
ranch.harvest.doc: Picks up the egg under the drone and holds it. If the drone's hands are full, it can't pick it up.
ranch.harvest.notes: An egg goes into storage only at the basket, with unload().
ranch.milk.doc: Milks the cow standing under the drone, if she's ready. The milk stays in the drone's hands.
ranch.milk.notes: A cow is ready when she's full and happy and her milk has filled up.
ranch.take.doc: On the basket tile, takes feed from storage; on the well tile, takes water. Without an amount, it takes as much as its hands can hold. Returns how much it took.
ranch.fill.doc: On the feed trough tile, pours the feed from its hands into the trough; on the water trough tile, the water. A trough holds 10.
ranch.unload.doc: On the basket tile, puts all the goods from its hands into storage (water gets poured out).
ranch.inHands.doc: How much of that item the drone is holding. Without an item, how much it's holding in total.
ranch.build.doc: Puts a feed trough (Machines.FeedTrough) or a water trough (Machines.WaterTrough) you've bought under the drone. The tile must be empty.
ranch.pet.doc: Pets the animals standing under the drone. They're happier for a minute.
ranch.clear.doc: Cleans the dirt off the tile under the drone.
ranch.dirt.doc: How dirty the tile under the drone is: from 0 to 100. Animals get sad on a dirty tile.
ranch.animals.doc: The list of animals in the drone's area. Each animal is an object: id, tesak (kind), x, y, sov (hunger), carav (thirst), tramadrutyun (mood), patrast (the cow is ready to milk).
ranch.price.doc: Today's price in ֏: for selling eggs and milk, and for buying grain and hay bales. The price changes every day and is the same for everyone.
ranch.sell.doc: The market drone sells eggs or milk from storage at today's price. Without an amount, it sells everything. Returns the ֏ it earned.
ranch.buy.doc: The market drone buys feed for ֏: Goods.Grain or Goods.HayBale. Returns how much it bought.
ranch.bring.doc: The market drone brings hay bales from the farm by cart: 10,000 wheat from the farm's Storage for each bale.
ranch.orders.doc: Today's list of orders. Each order is an object: anun is the name, irer the goods, gin the price, and katarvac tells if it's done.
ranch.deliver.doc: The market drone delivers the order with that number (the first one is 0), if storage has everything.
ranch.make.doc: In the workshop: the machine under the drone starts making the item, if there's enough inside (put it in with fill()). The dairy makes Matsun (Armenian yogurt), Cheese and Butter, the stove makes Omelet. You take what's ready with gather().
ranch.on.doc: The drone listens for the event and calls the function when it's free (its code has finished). The names are: "dzu" (a new egg), "kat" (a cow or goat is ready), "sovac" (an animal got hungry), "datark" (a trough is empty), "patrast" (a machine is ready), "ancq" (a hole in the fence), "grum" (someone wrote on the board), "esh" (the donkey arrived), "gorg" (the carpet is ready). The function gets an object: x, y and so on.
ranch.write.doc: Writes on the ranch's shared board, so every drone can read it. The value is a number, text, list or object (it gets copied).
ranch.read.doc: Reads from the board (null if there's no such name).
ranch.sellAnimal.doc: The market drone sells an animal by its id (from animals()). Babies can't be sold, and a rare color is expensive. Returns the ֏ it got.
ranch.heal.doc: Heals the sick animal standing under the drone, if the drone is holding medicine (Goods.Medicine).
ranch.repair.doc: On a tile next to the fence, fixes the hole with a plank (Goods.Plank in its hands).
ranch.rope.doc: On a tile next to the fence, when there are no holes, the drone brings back one runaway animal with a rope. It takes a few seconds.
ranch.ship.doc: The market drone takes goods to the farm by cart. Manure turns into humus (1 → 3), while eggs, milk, cheese and butter stay the same.
ranch.shear.doc: Takes wool from a ready sheep standing under the drone (only in the top right corner), and fluff from a rabbit (anywhere). Returns true or false.
ranch.bell.doc: Rings the bell on the drone's tile. The sheep come there and aren't scared for a few seconds.
ranch.moveDog.doc: The gampr (the Armenian shepherd dog) moves one tile. Sheep keep away from it, just like from the drone.
ranch.carpet.doc: On the loom tile, starts the carpet for an order (the number comes from carpetOrders()), and without a number, your own free carpet.
ranch.weave.doc: On the loom tile, weaves one knot (one second and one yarn). x and y go from 0 to 8, and (0, 0) is the bottom left corner. A knot can't be changed. The 81st knot finishes the carpet.
ranch.carpetOrders.doc: Today's list of carpet orders. Each order is an object: anun is the name, makardak the level, gin the price, and vercvac tells if it's taken. The patterns are shown in the "Loom" window.
ranch.sellCarpet.doc: The market drone sells all the finished carpets. Returns the ֏ it earned.
ranch.plant.doc: In the apiary, plants a flower under the drone. The drone must be holding a seed (Goods.Seed). wipe() removes the flower.
ranch.flowerKinds.doc: How many different flowers there are around the drone, up to 2 tiles away. The hive fills up that many times faster.
ranch.eat.doc: All the ranch drones get faster for a while. The food, an omelet or a honey cake, comes from storage.
ranch.donkeyBring.doc: The donkey brings a load from the farm (at the same prices as the cart). Works from any area, one trip at a time. Returns the amount. When it arrives, when("esh", …) is called.
ranch.donkeyShip.doc: The donkey takes goods to the farm (just like ship()). The goods arrive at the end of the trip.
ranch.fair.doc: The market drone delivers all the goods and one good unsold carpet to the fair. To see what's needed, look in the "Market" window.
ranch.festivalDistance.doc: On festival days, tells you how many steps it is to the nearest object hidden in this area (null if there's no festival).
ranch.digPond.doc: On festival days, digs up the object hidden under the drone. On the wrong tile, the nearest object runs away.
js.basics.title: Commands, () and ;
js.basics.about: Code is a list of commands. The computer runs them one by one, from top to bottom. Every command has a name, parentheses (), and a semicolon ; at the end. Inside the parentheses we sometimes write what the command should work with.
js.basics.mistakes.0: Capital and small letters are different: Flip() and flip() are two different names.
js.basics.mistakes.1: Don't forget the (): without parentheses the command won't run.
js.basics.mistakes.2: A period . doesn't end a line of code: put ; at the end of the line.
js.comments.title: Comments //
js.comments.about: After //, the rest of the line is a comment: the computer doesn't read it. With comments you leave notes for yourself in your code. You can also "switch off" a line by putting // at its start.
js.comments.mistakes.0: If you put // in front of a command, the command won't run.
js.while.title: while loop
js.while.about: while means "as long as". As long as the condition in the parentheses is true, the commands inside the curly braces { } repeat. while (true) repeats forever, until you press "Stop".
js.while.mistakes.0: Don't forget to close the curly brace }.
js.while.mistakes.1: The condition goes in parentheses: while (true), not while true.
js.while.mistakes.2: Commands written after an endless loop will never run.
js.for.title: for loop
js.for.about: for repeats code a set number of times. It has three parts, separated by ;: the start (let i = 0), the condition (i < 5) and the step (i++). i is a counter that gets bigger on every round.
js.for.mistakes.1: i < 3 means 0, 1, 2 (three times): 3 itself isn't included.
js.breakContinue.title: break and continue
js.breakContinue.about: break jumps out of the loop right away. continue skips the rest of this round and moves on to the next one.
js.breakContinue.mistakes.0: break and continue work only inside a loop.
js.if.about: if checks a condition. If it's true, the commands inside the if's { } run. else ("otherwise") runs when the condition isn't true. You can add else if for one more condition.
js.if.mistakes.1: Don't put ; after the if's parentheses, or the if will do nothing.
js.booleans.title: true and false
js.booleans.about: true means "yes, that's right", and false means "no, that's wrong". Commands like isRipe() and comparisons (5 > 3) answer true or false. That's exactly what goes in the conditions of if and while.
js.booleans.mistakes.0: true and false are written in small letters and without quotes.
js.math.title: Arithmetic
js.math.about: + adds, - subtracts, * multiplies, / divides, and % gives the remainder of a division. Just like in math class, * and / are done before + and -, and parentheses change the order.
js.compare.title: Comparison
js.compare.about: == checks if two things are equal, != if they're different, and < > <= >= mean less than, greater than, less than or equal to, greater than or equal to. The answer is true or false.
js.compare.mistakes.0: To compare, write ==. A single = sign puts a value in a variable.
js.logic.title: &&, || and !
js.logic.about: && ("and") is true if both conditions are true. || ("or") is true if at least one is true. ! ("not") flips the answer: !true is false.
js.logic.mistakes.0: Write && and || as two symbols with no space between them.
js.variables.title: Variables (let, const)
js.variables.about: A variable is a box with a name, where we keep a value. let makes a variable you can change, and const makes one that doesn't change. The = sign puts a new value in the box.
js.variables.mistakes.0: Write let only the first time, when you create the variable.
js.variables.mistakes.1: A name can't have spaces: write harvestCount or harvest_count.
js.console.title: console.log and alert
js.console.about: console.log() writes to the console: it's the real JavaScript name of say(). alert() shows text in a window, and the code waits until you close it. Both help you see what your code is doing.
js.console.mistakes.0: Put a dot after console: console.log.
js.console.mistakes.1: In an endless loop, alert() opens the window again and again: stop the code with the window's "Stop" button.
js.update.title: ++ and +=
js.update.about: i++ is the same as i = i + 1. i-- is i = i - 1. x += 5 is the same as x = x + 5. They're just shorter ways to write it.
js.update.mistakes.0: ++ works only with a variable: you can't write 5++.
js.text.title: Text
js.text.about: Text goes inside quotes: "like this" or 'like this'. You can join pieces of text with +. Inside backticks (`…`), ${…} puts in a variable's value.
js.text.mistakes.0: Curly quotes “like these” don't work in code: use " or '.
js.text.mistakes.1: A number in quotes becomes text: "2" + "2" is "22".
js.functions.title: Functions
js.functions.about: A function is your own command. You create it with the word function, and it runs only when you call it by its name with (). Functions make code short and easy to understand.
js.functions.mistakes.0: Creating a function doesn't run it yet: don't forget to call it.
js.functions.mistakes.1: Don't give a function the same name as a game command.
js.params.title: Parameters and return
js.params.about: A function can get values (parameters) in its parentheses. return ends the function and gives back an answer you can use.
js.params.mistakes.0: Commands written after return won't run.
js.arrow.title: Arrow functions =>
js.arrow.about: You can also write a function the short way, with the => arrow. It's kept in a variable.
js.arrow.mistakes.0: => is written with = and >, with no space between them.
js.lists.title: Lists
js.lists.about: A list (an array) keeps many values in one variable. Its elements are numbered from 0, so a list's [0] is the first one. length is the number of elements, and push() adds an element at the end.
js.lists.mistakes.0: The first element is list[0], not list[1].
js.forOf.about: for…of goes through all the elements of a list, one by one. On each round, the variable gets the next element.
js.forOf.mistakes.0: of and in are different: for a list, use of.
js.objects.title: Objects
js.objects.about: An object keeps values by name (by key). You get a value with a dot, object.key, or with square brackets, object["key"].
js.objects.mistakes.0: Put : between a key and its value, and , between the pairs.
js.mapSet.title: Map and Set
js.mapSet.about: A Map keeps key → value pairs, where the key can be any value (for example, a plant). A Set keeps only values that don't repeat. You create both with new.
js.mapSet.mistakes.0: For a Map, use .get() and .set(), not a dot and the key.
js.import.title: import and export
js.import.about: You can split your code into several files. export makes a function or variable available to other files, and import brings it in from another file.
js.import.mistakes.0: Write the file name in quotes, without .js.
js.import.mistakes.1: The function must be exported, or import won't find it.
js.mathLib.title: Math and random numbers
js.mathLib.about: Math has ready-made math functions, and Math.random() gives a random number from 0 up to 1 (but never 1 itself).
js.mathLib.mistakes.0: Math is written with a capital M.
js.numbers.title: Number ↔ text
js.numbers.about: parseInt() turns text into a whole number, parseFloat() into a decimal number, and String() turns a number into text. isNaN() checks whether a value is not a number.
js.numbers.mistakes.0: parseInt("12abc") is 12, but parseInt("abc") is NaN (not a number).
plants.Grass.about: Wheat is the simplest plant. It grows by itself on every empty meadow tile, ripens in half a second and gives wheat when you gather it.
plants.Grass.tips: You don't need to plant wheat: after you gather it, it grows back on the meadow, and gather() doesn't hurt unripe wheat. Each level of the "Wheat" research doubles the harvest.
plants.Bush.about: Rosehips give wood. They grow in any soil in a few seconds.
plants.Bush.tips: After you gather, the tile is empty, so plant again. If you gather an unripe rosehip, it's lost with no harvest.
plants.Tree.about: An apricot tree gives more wood than a rosehip, but grows slower. One tree gives a harvest three times.
plants.Tree.tips: scan() tells you how many harvests the tree has left (3, 2 or 1). The second and third harvests ripen faster. After the last harvest the tree disappears, and you need to plant a new one.
plants.Mulberry.about: A mulberry tree gives wood, and after you gather it you need to plant a new one. It loves bees.
plants.Mulberry.tips: If there's a ripe rosehip next to the mulberry tree (up, down, right or left) when you gather it, the wood doubles. Plant mulberry trees and rosehips in a checkerboard pattern, and don't gather those rosehips!
plants.Carrot.about: Eggplants grow only in plowed soil and are planted from seeds (Goods.Seeds).
plants.Carrot.tips: First plow(), then sow(Plants.Eggplant). Your first seeds come from wheat (about once in every 20 times you gather it), and every ripe eggplant gives back 1–3 seeds. If you gather it unripe, the seed is lost.
plants.Pumpkin.about: Watermelons grow in plowed soil, and planting one costs an eggplant. Once grown, a watermelon gets sweeter, and then it rots.
plants.Pumpkin.tips: scan() gives the sweetness (0–100). Gather it when it's 80–100. If you gather it earlier, you get nothing, and about 12 seconds after 100 the watermelon rots (Plants.RottenWatermelon). Plant a new one in the rotten one's place.
plants.YellowMelon.about: Yellow watermelons grow in plowed soil. A ripe one sends tendrils to the empty plowed soil next to it, and a new one grows there.
plants.YellowMelon.tips: One gather() picks up all the ripe ones that touch each other, and n of them give n² watermelons. Plant one, wait for the patch to grow, then gather.
plants.SquareMelon.about: Square watermelons grow in plowed soil, and planting one costs an eggplant.
plants.SquareMelon.tips: A square of ripe square watermelons side by side joins into one giant: an n×n giant gives n³ watermelons (from 6×6 up, 6·n²). You gather the giant with one gather().
plants.Sunflower.about: Pomegranates grow in plowed soil and give pomegranate juice (Goods.Juice). With drink(), the drone drinks one juice and does 50 actions 2 times faster.
plants.Sunflower.tips: scan() tells you the number of seeds (1–30). Only pomegranates with an even number of seeds give juice. If each even one has more seeds than the even one before it, the juice goes up: 1, 2, 3… An odd one gives no juice and spills one juice from your Storage.
plants.Cactus.about: Grapes grow in plowed soil and have a sweetness from 0 to 9 (scan()). Planting them costs a watermelon.
plants.Cactus.tips: If the ripe grapes side by side in a row never get smaller from left to right, one gather() picks up the whole row, and n grapes give n². Swap them around with exchange(Right) or exchange(Left).
plants.Mushroom.about: Mushrooms give magic dust. A ripe mushroom hides to the right or left, so you have to tell gather() which side to look on: Right or Left.
plants.Mushroom.tips: If you look on the wrong side, the mushroom runs away with no harvest. It remembers your last choices and learns anything that repeats, so choose at random. That way, you'll get about half of the mushrooms.
plants.11.title: Water
plants.11.about: Water (Goods.Water) comes by itself every few seconds. use(Goods.Water) waters the soil under the drone, and plants grow up to 5 times faster.
plants.11.tips: waterLevel() shows how wet the soil is (0–1). Water dries up, so water again.
plants.12.title: Pond and fish
plants.12.about: Dig a pond with dig() and fill it with water until waterLevel() becomes 1. In a full pond, goFishing() catches a random fish: carp (often), barbel (sometimes), ishkhan, the Lake Sevan trout (rarely), or goldfish (very rarely).
plants.12.tips: After a catch the pond rests a little (it stops sparkling), so more ponds and more drones mean more fish. Fish are needed for the last "Speed" levels, for "Mushrooms" and for the bakery. Your first goldfish unlocks the fisher hat.
plants.13.title: Humus and tired soil
plants.13.about: Humus (Goods.Humus) gives a growing plant 2 seconds of growth at once and makes tired soil strong again.
plants.13.tips: Soil gets tired when you keep harvesting the same plant on the same tile: the harvest drops by up to half, and the soil turns pale. Switch between different plants, and the soil will rest.
plants.14.title: Maze
plants.14.about: A maze is planted with sow(Plants.Maze) and covers the whole farm, with treasure inside (Plants.Treasure). It uses the mushrooms' magic dust: as much as the length of the farm's side. Too little dust means a smaller maze.
plants.14.tips: scan() gives the treasure's [x, y], and canGo() tells you if there's a wall. When you gather the treasure, you get gold.
plants.15.title: Snake
plants.15.about: With the snake hat, the drone turns into a snake that hunts the mouse (Plants.Mouse). Every mouse it catches makes its tail longer.
plants.15.tips: scan() gives the mouse's position. The mouse runs away on every second step of the snake, so chase it into a corner. The snake can't cross its own tail. When you take the hat off, you get snake skin: the number of mice times the snake's length.
